title: Streamflow CI regression oracle with slice-capturer for tokens/sec and p95
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: PRs that touch runtime scheduling, kernel selection, or batching frequently introduce regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency that only appear under realistic bursty traffic. Current CI guards are either too coarse (single global threshold) or too expensive (full replay). Goal: build a lightweight, streaming regression oracle for PR gating that captures stratified micro-slices of production-like load, computes stable tokens/sec and p95 baselines per-slice, and produces explainable pass/fail decisions for PRs with tunable sensitivity and cost budget.
implementation_notes: Introduce a Slice Capturer that samples short traffic windows (10s-60s) across frequency/sequence-length/model axes and persists compact traces (metadata + token counts + p95 samples).

Build a Streamflow Oracle service in CI that replays sampled slices in a low-cost emulator using reduced replicas and synthetic KV cache warmup to approximate steady-path p95 and tokens/sec without full cluster replay.

Use bootstrap aggregation across 3 independent runs per PR to estimate median and 95% CI for tokens/sec and p95; flag regressions using a combined effect size + p-value policy to reduce false positives on noisy slices.
Provide per-slice annotations in the PR UI with trace links, delta breakdown (scheduling, kernel time, batch efficiency), and suggested mitigation (reduce batch, knob tweak, revert kernel change).
Make sensitivity configurable by PR label (quick-smoke vs full-gate) and enforce a max-cost budget per PR (credits charged to author org).

Trade-offs considered: higher sensitivity increases CI cost and false positives; using compact sampling reduces fidelity for long-tail microbursts. We favor a multi-slice fusion approach to balance both.
Instrumentation: extend existing perf-agent to emit compact histograms of token latency and per-batch kernel timings; add a small SDK shim to simulate KV cache hit patterns.
Data retention: samples retained for 90 days; older slices aggregated into baselines for long-term drift analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Streamflow CI job runs on PRs touching runtime or models and completes within configured budget (default 15 minutes / $3 equivalent).
Oracle produces deterministic pass/fail decisions with recorded evidence (links to stored slices and delta reports) for at least 90% of tested slices.
False positive rate measured on historical non-regressing PRs is < 3% across the main model family (gpt-like-13b) during canary window.
Delta report surfaces top-3 contributing factors (kernel, batching, cache) and a recommended follow-up task or knob to try.
Documentation and PR UI integration completed: Confluence runbook, example PR comment template, and a Grafana dashboard for streamflow job health.
comments: 2026-03-08 - Kickoff: scope agreed with TL and PM. Focus first on tokens/sec + p95 for transformer encoder-decoder family and generalize later.
2026-03-09 - Design review: agreed to avoid full load replays; opted for stratified short-slice sampling. Action: Ravi to prototype slice capturer agent (ENG-164512).
2026-03-10 - Probe results: initial emulator underestimates p95 for cold-KV cases by ~18%. Decided to add synthetic KV warmup phase (30s) to emulator and to annotate slices with cache-hit profile.
2026-03-11 - PR UI mockups posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Streamflow+-+PR+UI (internal). Requesting design feedback from @Maya Chen.

2026-03-12 - Interim run: ran Streamflow on three historical PRs (two regressions, one noop). Oracle flagged both regressions and withheld one noop. Logging false-positive candidate for further tuning; linked traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rJXQ/streamflow-traces?var-job=ENG-164501
2026-03-12 - Blocker identified: infra quota prevents parallel emulator forks for large PR batches. Raised dependency on infra team (ENG-165020).
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on the statistical decision rule in implementation_notes (combined effect size + p-value) — we prefer fewer false alarms at the cost of slightly reduced sensitivity.
Check cost estimation in the CI job template; current budget targets $3/PR for the quick-smoke path and $12/PR for full-gate.
Design/PM: confirm PR UI text for explainability and suggested next steps (revert, tweak knob, open follow-up ticket).
